text: First written record, as Scinna: the king gives the village to Jakov, county head of Uzhhorod.
First written record, as Solmus, in a charter of King Sigismund.
Senné has at least 25 serf households, Iňačovce at least 19.
Senné: 26 serf houses, a manor, a church and a rectory. Iňačovce: 32 serf houses.
Rákóczi's rising. The Latin parishes of the county have to be rebuilt afterwards, Senné among them.
Tax census: 5 households in Senné, 8 in Iňačovce.
Roman Catholic church rebuilt on old foundations.
Tax census: 11 households in each village. After this Iňačovce is refilled from the north of Ung and Zemplín.
List of parishes, then the bishop of Eger's visitation. Senné is a Latin parish with eight filials. Iňačovce has its own Greek Catholic parish, where Rusyn is spoken.
Reformed register begins.
Urbarial survey: 26 villein households in Senné, 35 in Iňačovce. Baron István Vécsey is the main landlord of both.
Greek Catholic eparchy of Mukachevo erected; the bishop sits at Uzhhorod.
A water mill on an arm of the Uh is first recorded.
The Roman Catholic parishes of Ung county pass from Eger to the new diocese of Szatmár.
Augustín Roškováni, later bishop of Vác and of Nitra, is born in the manor to an estate employee's family.
Greek Catholic register begins.
Land census: Senné 120 houses and 833 people; Iňačovce 119 houses and 1,023 people.
Surviving Roman Catholic register begins.
The bishop of Szatmár's circulars are copied into a parish book: the Duska agent's Folder 1.
Serfdom abolished. In Senné each holding keeps about 13 hectares; labour dues for forest and pasture run on until the 1896 buy-out law.
Schools: Roman Catholic in Senné, 61 pupils. Greek Catholic, 69 pupils, and Reformed, 14 pupils, in Iňačovce.
First full census of Hungary. The Ung county sheets are now at Berehove.
First wave of emigration.
State civil registration begins on 1 October.
Second wave of emigration, mostly to the United States. Many return to buy land.
The Reformed build their own church.
Treaty of Trianon, 4 June. The villages are in Czechoslovakia; the names Senné and Iňačovce become official.
Land reform begins to break up the Vécsey estate. Iňačovce is placed in the Michalovce district.
Baron László Vécsey dies; the estate passes to his nephew Mihály Sztáray.
The slump hits the farms that had mortgaged themselves to buy estate land.
Czechoslovak census, by household and house number.
Mobilisation in September. On 2 November the First Vienna Award returns Uzhhorod to Hungary.
Little War, 23 to 31 March. Slovak volunteers hold Senné; an air fight is seen over the village. The new border runs about 2 km away.
Senné: 171 houses, 839 people. Iňačovce: 190 houses, 747 people. About 600 cows die in Senné and harvests fail until 1942.
The church chronicle records hunger: "Niet nieže chleba, ale ani zemiakov" (not only no bread, not even potatoes).
Register of Jews: 20 people in Senné, 13 in Iňačovce. Four families are deported from Senné.
Hungarian then German troops in the village from 28 October; fields flooded; a machine-gun post in the church tower. Soviet soldiers enter on 27 November.
Czechoslovakia restored. Uzhhorod and the eastern part of old Ung county pass to the Soviet Union.
The Senné fishponds reserve is declared, in the fields of Iňačovce and Senné.
Farm cooperative founded on 30 January, the last in the district.
Moved from the Veľké Kapušany district to Michalovce.
